 136| **Setup.** We observe D_n = {(x_i, y_i) : i = 1, …, n}: n independent copies of a pair (x, y), where x ∈ ℝ^p is a
 137| vector of p predictors and y is a real response. The number of predictors p may grow with n and may be much larger
 138| than n; the law of (x, y) may change with n.
 139| 
 140| *What the method does.* (1) It removes the predictors that are constant in the sample, and centres and scales every
 141| other predictor, and the response, by its sample mean and sample standard deviation. Let r be the number of predictors
 142| that remain (r ≤ p). (2) On the standardised data it uses one fixed prior, with no tuning parameter: the number of
 143| included predictors has the beta-binomial BB(1, r) distribution restricted to at most min(r, ⌊n/2⌋), and given that
 144| number all sets S of that size are equally likely; given S and the noise variance, the coefficients of the predictors
 145| in S are jointly normal with mean zero and covariance n × (noise variance) × (G_S + I)⁻¹, where G_S is the sample Gram
 146| matrix of the standardised predictors in S and I is the identity matrix of the same size; the noise variance has an
 147| inverse-gamma prior with shape 0.01 and rate 0.01. (3) The posterior is mapped back to the original units.
 148| Π(· | D_n) denotes the resulting posterior distribution of (S, β, σ²): S is the set of included predictors, β ∈ ℝ^p the
 149| coefficient vector in the original units (zero outside S and for removed predictors), and σ² the noise variance in the
 150| original units. If fewer than two predictors remain, or the response is constant in the sample, the posterior is not
 151| defined here; under the assumptions below such data sets have probability smaller than the exceptional probabilities
 152| in the theorems and are counted in them: there the posterior probabilities in the displays are read as 1. The common exceptional set of the proofs also contains every data set with r < p.
 153| 
 154| *The distribution attached to a posterior draw.* A draw (S, β, σ²) defines a joint density f for a new pair (x, y): x
 155| has its true distribution and, given x, y is normal with mean ȳ + (x − x̄)ᵀβ and variance σ², where ȳ and x̄ are the
 156| sample means of the response and of the predictors. f* is the true joint density of (x, y).
 157| 
 158| *Notation.* d_H(f, g) = (1 − ∫√(fg))^{1/2} is the Hellinger distance between two densities. P* is the distribution of the
 159| data D_n. sd(·), Var(·) and Corr(·) are population standard deviations, variances and correlation matrices.
 160| z_j = (x_j − E x_j)/sd(x_j) is the j-th standardised predictor and z = (z_1, …, z_p). For a set T of predictors, x_T is
 161| the sub-vector of x. λ_min(·) is the smallest eigenvalue of a symmetric matrix. |S| is the number of predictors in S.
 162| log is the natural logarithm.
 163| 
 164| **Constants, the level M and the window q_n.** s ≥ 0 is an integer and A ≥ 1, K ≥ 1, c_ψ > 0, b̄ > 0 are constants; none
 165| depends on n. Fix a number M ≥ 1, the *level*: a larger M gives a larger ball and a smaller exceptional probability.
 166| The *window* is
 167| 
 168|     q_n = min{ p, ⌈C_q·M·log n⌉ },   where C_q = 2(s(A + 2) + 4)/log 2.
 169| 
 170| It is the largest number of predictors that assumptions (A3) and (A4) constrain jointly; for a fixed level M it is of
 171| order log n. (K below is the constant of (A3); the cap on the model size is always written min(r, ⌊n/2⌋).)
 172| 
 173| **Assumptions.**
 174| - **(A1) Gaussian linear model.** y = α* + xᵀβ* + ε, where ε is normal with mean 0 and variance σ*² > 0 and is independent
 175|   of x. (α*, β*, σ* and the law of x may depend on n.)
 176| - **(A2) Sparsity and dimension.** At most s coordinates of β* are nonzero, and 2 ≤ p ≤ n^A.
 177| - **(A3) Sub-Gaussian predictors.** Every predictor has positive variance, and for every vector u ∈ ℝ^p with at most q_n
 178|   nonzero entries and every real λ:   E exp(λ·uᵀz) ≤ exp(K²λ²·Var(uᵀz)/2).
 179| - **(A4) No near-exact collinearity.** For every set T of at most q_n predictors:   λ_min(Corr(x_T)) ≥ c_ψ/n.
 180| - **(A5) Bounded signal.** |β*_j|·sd(x_j) ≤ b̄·σ* for every j.
 181| No lower bound on the nonzero coefficients is assumed (no beta-min condition), and no fixed lower bound on
 182| eigenvalues: under (A4) predictors may be correlated up to 1 − c_ψ/n. ((A4) still makes sparse coefficient vectors
 183| distinguishable in principle; the statement without (A4) below needs no such condition.)
 184| 
 185| **Theorem A (the posterior recovers the joint distribution of predictors and response).** There are constants c > 0,
 186| C₁, M₀ and n₀, depending only on (s, A, K, c_ψ, b̄), such that the following holds whenever n ≥ n₀, M₀ ≤ M ≤ √n/log n and
 187| (A1)–(A5) hold with the window q_n of this M:
 188| 
 189|     (i)   P*[ Π( d_H(f, f*) > √(M·log n / n) | D_n ) > n^{−cM} ] ≤ n^{−cM},
 190| 
 191|     (ii)  P*[ Π( |S| > s + C₁·M | D_n ) > n^{−cM} ] ≤ n^{−cM}.
 192| 
 193| In words. (i) Except on a set of data sets of probability at most n^{−cM}, the posterior gives probability at most
 194| n^{−cM} to joint distributions farther than √(M log n/n) from the truth in Hellinger distance: the posterior contracts
 195| at the rate √(log n/n). (ii) On the same data sets the posterior gives probability at most n^{−cM} to models with more
 196| than s + C₁M predictors. Statement (ii) bounds the number of selected predictors; it does not say that they are the
 197| true ones. The two exceptional sets of data sets can be taken to be the same set. The bounds are uniform over all laws
 198| of the data that satisfy (A1)–(A5) with the given constants.
 199| 
 200| *Without (A4).* If (A4) is dropped, and (A3) is required only for single predictors (vectors u with one nonzero
 201| entry), then (i) holds with the radius √(M·log n·log(p ∨ n)/n), which is larger by the factor √(log(p ∨ n)), and (ii) holds
 202| with s + C₁·M·log n in place of s + C₁·M. (Here p ∨ n is the larger of p and n.)
 203| 
 204| *Example.* Jointly Gaussian predictors satisfy (A3) with K = 1; independent predictors satisfy it when each of them
 205| satisfies it with a common constant K. (A4) holds for all large n whenever every q_n × q_n principal block of the correlation matrix has
 206| smallest eigenvalue at least a fixed ψ > 0: for instance correlation ρ^{|j−k|} with |ρ| < 1, or equal correlation
 207| ρ ∈ [0, 1).
 208| 
 209| **Theorem B (parametric rate when the true predictors are detectable).** Assume (A1)–(A5) with the window q_n of M = 1
 210| and with exactly s ≥ 1 nonzero coordinates of β*, **and in addition**
 211| - **(A6) Detectable signal.** (a) λ_min(Corr(x_T)) ≥ ψ for a constant ψ > 0 and every set T of at most (2A + 3)s + 2
 212|   predictors; (b) min{ |β*_j|·sd(x_j)/σ* : β*_j ≠ 0 } ≥ b_n, where b_n > 0 and b_n²·n/log n → ∞.
 213| Then for every sequence M_n → ∞:
 214| 
 215|     Π( d_H(f, f*) > M_n/√n | D_n ) → 0   in P*-probability.
 216| 
 217| **Corollary C (the output of the sampler).** The method uses a sequential Monte Carlo sampler to explore the models and to compute summaries
 218| of the posterior; it does not compute the full posterior
 219| (small problems that it solves by exact enumeration are not covered here). A run is *completed* when the method
 220| reports the status "completed"; runs that stop early are not covered. The output of a completed run contains a list 𝒯
 221| of at most 40r + 1 distinct models: the best-scoring models among those offered to the final run of the sampler —
 222| the models scored in that run, together with models the method scored earlier and carries into it (its precomputed
 223| tables for small groups of predictors, and models kept from its calibration stage). Each model in the list comes with
 224| the logarithm of its unnormalised posterior weight, which we take to be computed in exact arithmetic. The output
 225| contains no draws of (β, σ²). Let π(𝒯) be the posterior probability of the list, and let Π̂ — not computed by the method —
 226| be the posterior restricted to the list: the models in 𝒯, weighted in proportion to the exponentials of their returned
 227| log-weights, each with its exact conditional posterior distribution of (β, σ²). Under the conditions of Theorem A,
 228| with P*-probability at least 1 − n^{−cM} over the data, **every** completed run (whatever its random numbers) with
 229| π(𝒯) ≥ n^{−cM/2} satisfies
 230| 
 231|     Π̂( d_H(f, f*) > √(M·log n / n) ) ≤ n^{−cM/2}.
 232| 
 233| If a completed run scored the true model {j : β*_j ≠ 0} and the posterior probability of that model exceeds ½, then the
 234| list contains it, it is the model the method reports as most probable, and π(𝒯) > ½. More generally π(𝒯) is the total
 235| posterior probability of the listed models, and no single model needs to carry most of it: the posterior is in general
 236| a mixture over many models (typically the true model together with many models that add one predictor to it), and the
 237| condition above concerns the list as a whole. Whether the list carries enough posterior probability is a property of the
 238| run: this corollary does not assert it, and the output does not certify it.

 143| - (a) If Q is a law on Ω and L ∈ [0, ∞) satisfies Q(S) ≤ Lπ(S) for every S ∈ Ω, then QΠ(B) ≤ LΠ(B | D_n).

 151| **Lemma P6(c) (mixture convexity; used for the predictive bounds).** Let Q be a probability on 𝚯 and let A ⊆ 𝚯 be
 152| measurable with d_H²(f_ξ, f*) ≤ ε² for every ξ ∈ 𝚯 ∖ A. Then f̄_Q is a density with respect to ν_x ⊗ Leb, and
 153| d_H²(f̄_Q, f*) ≤ ∫ d_H²(f_ξ, f*) Q(dξ) ≤ ε² + Q(A).
 154| 
 155| *Proof.* Write μ := ν_x ⊗ Leb and g_ξ(x, y) := φ(y; â_ξ + xᵀb_ξ, v_ξ), so that f_ξ = g_ξ μ-a.e. and f* = φ(y; α* + xᵀβ*, σ*²).
 156| On each piece {S} × ℝ^S × (0, ∞), the map (θ, v, x, y) ↦ g_ξ(x, y) is continuous: b_ξ is linear in θ, â_ξ = ȳ^r − x̄ᵀb_ξ,
 157| and φ is continuous for v > 0. So (ξ, x, y) ↦ g_ξ(x, y) is jointly measurable, and Tonelli applies to nonnegative
 158| integrands. (1) ∫ f̄_Q dμ = ∫ (∫ g_ξ dμ) Q(dξ) = 1. (2) For each (x, y), √· is concave and Q is a probability, so Jensen
 159| gives √(f̄_Q(x, y)) ≥ ∫ √(g_ξ(x, y)) Q(dξ). Multiply by √f* ≥ 0, integrate in μ and use Tonelli:

 163| ## 4. Code lemmas (what the returned store is)
 164| 
 165| Fix the data and the streams, assume EX-A, and suppose the run is completed.
 166| 
 167| **Definition (order).** For S, S′ ∈ Ω write S ≺ S′ ("S ranks before S′") iff F(S) > F(S′); or F(S) = F(S′) and
 168| |S| < |S′|; or F(S) = F(S′), |S| = |S′| and `lex_less`(S, S′) (models are sorted index vectors; P14). For distinct sorted
 169| vectors exactly one of `lex_less`(S, S′), `lex_less`(S′, S) holds (`std::lexicographical_compare` is a strict total
 170| order on finite sequences). F is real-valued under EX-A. So ≺ is a strict total order on Ω. For A ⊆ Ω and an integer
 171| k ≥ 1, top_k(A) denotes the set of the min(k, |A|) ≺-first elements of A.
 172| 
 173| **Lemma R0 (the comparators are ≺).** (i) If entries have the form (F(S), S), then `TopCmp{true}`(e, e′) holds iff S ≺ S′
 174| (P11). Entries e, e′ are equivalent for `std::set` (neither compares less) iff S = S′. (ii) `hpm_better`(F(S), S, F(S′), S′)
 175| holds iff S ≺ S′ (P14).
 176| *Proof.* (i) `TopCmp` returns `a.v > b.v` when the values differ, then `a.S.size() < b.S.size()` when the sizes differ,
 177| then `lex_less(a.S, b.S)`. With v = F(S) this is the definition of ≺. Since ≺ is a strict total order, neither
 178| S ≺ S′ nor S′ ≺ S holds iff S = S′. (ii) `hpm_better` makes the same three comparisons in the same order. ∎
 179| 
 180| Every entry offered to the final-run store has v = F(S) exactly. Offers come from `offer_stores(S, F, …)` with the F
 181| computed by `eval` (P15), from the block tables (P19: `F = logprior[|U|] + logm_tab`), or from inherited models (P20:
 182| `logprior[|S|] + sc.score(S).logm`). Under EX-A each of these is the exact F(S) of (H-ID).
 183| 
 184| **Definition (𝓜).** 𝓜 is the set of models S for which `offer_stores` is called on the final-run ledger `led`
 185| (P18) during the run. On a completed run `top.offer` is called only inside `offer_stores` (P12; the only other `offer`
 186| call, `cpp/v3_core.cpp:549`, belongs to the exact enumeration on its own store). `offer_hpm` is called only inside
 187| `offer_stores` (P23). So 𝓜 is also exactly the set offered to the running HPM.
 188| 
 189| **Lemma R (store invariant).** Let A_m be the set of models offered by the first m calls of `top.offer`, and s_m the
 190| set of models in `top.s` after these calls. Then s_m = top_k(A_m) for every m, where k = 40p_ret + 1 ≥ 81. In
 191| particular the returned 𝒯 = top_k(𝓜), listed in ≺-order (P7: `store_to_list` iterates the set in comparator order).
 192| 
 193| *Proof.* Induction on m. m = 0: s_0 = ∅ = top_k(∅) (`init` builds an empty set, P8). Step: call m + 1 offers e = (F(S), S).
 194| Write A := A_m, s := s_m = top_k(A), A′ := A ∪ {S}. The code (P10) does the following. If |s| ≥ k and not
 195| `cmp`(e, last(s)), it returns. Else, if `s.count(e)` (an equivalent entry is present, i.e. S ∈ s by R0(i)), it returns.
 196| Otherwise it inserts e and, if then |s| > k, erases the ≺-last element. (`*s.rbegin()` and `std::prev(s.end())` are
 197| the ≺-last element of the set.) Note |s| ≤ k always, so "|s| ≥ k" means |s| = k.
 198| - Case 1: S ∈ A. Then A′ = A, and we must show s is unchanged. If the code inserted e, then S ∉ s and (|s| < k or
 199|   S ≺ last(s)). If |s| < k, then s = top_k(A) = A, so S ∈ s: contradiction. If |s| = k and S ≺ last(s): S ∈ A ∖ s and
 200|   s = top_k(A) imply that every element of s ranks before S, in particular last(s) ≺ S: contradiction. So the code
 201|   returned without change, and s_{m+1} = s = top_k(A′).
 202| - Case 2: S ∉ A, |s| = k and not (S ≺ last(s)). Since S ≠ last(s) and ≺ is total, last(s) ≺ S. So S ranks after all k
 203|   elements of s, and top_k(A′) = s. The code returns at the quick-reject line without change.
 204| - Case 3: S ∉ A, and (|s| < k or S ≺ last(s)). S ∉ s, so `count` is 0 and e is inserted. (3a) If |s| < k then s = A, so
 205|   s ∪ {S} = A′ with |A′| ≤ k. Nothing is erased, and s_{m+1} = A′ = top_k(A′). (3b) If |s| = k and S ≺ last(s), then
 206|   |s ∪ {S}| = k + 1 and the code erases the ≺-last element of s ∪ {S}. That element is last(s), because S ≺ last(s).
 207|   So s_{m+1} = (s ∖ {last(s)}) ∪ {S}. This is top_k(A′): every T ∈ A ∖ s ranks after all of s (since s = top_k(A)), so
 208|   at least k elements of A′ rank before T and T ∉ top_k(A′); hence top_k(A′) ⊆ s ∪ {S}, and among these k + 1
 209|   elements the ≺-last one, last(s), is excluded. ∎

 211| **Lemma M (what 𝓜 contains).** On a completed run, 𝓜 = 𝓜_tab ∪ 𝓜_inh ∪ 𝓜_eval, where:
 212| - 𝓜_tab is the set of block-table models with a score (P19, P32);
 213| - 𝓜_inh is the set of inherited models (P20); these are the models of the calibration's three stores
 214|   (`cpp/v3_core.cpp:728-735`);
 215| - 𝓜_eval is the set of models on which the final-run engine calls `eval` (with either value of `emit`) or `held`: the
 216|   islands' initial draws, Gibbs flips and held states, swap and independence proposals (accepted or rejected), and
 217|   every model scanned or used as a centre by the final local search and LS0.
 218| 
 219| Also ∅ ∈ 𝓜 (the empty code of every block table, P19), so 𝓜 ≠ ∅, and 𝓜 ⊆ Ω.
 220| 
 221| *Proof.* "⊆": by the Definition, offers are made only by `event` with `is_fresh` true (P13), which `eval`, `held` and
 222| `ingest_tables` call, and by the inherited loop (P20). Each of these offers a model in 𝓜_tab ∪ 𝓜_inh ∪ 𝓜_eval.
 223| "⊇": 𝓜_tab and 𝓜_inh are offered directly (P19 with `is_fresh = true`; P20). Take S ∈ 𝓜_eval, and look at the first
 224| `eval`/`held` call on S in the final run.
 225| - (a) A `held` call re-emits the current state of a particle. That state was set either by `set_model` followed by
 226|   `eval(P[i], ME_INIT)` with `emit = true` (`cpp/v3_engine.h:290-291`), or by copying `tmpQ` (`:131, 158, 179, 191`),
 227|   which was just `eval`ed with `emit = true` (`:122, 153, 174, 186`). So an `eval` with `emit = true` on S precedes it.
 228| - (b) An `eval` with `emit = true` either misses the cache — then `fresh = true` and the event offers S (P15, P13) — or
 229|   hits it. The cache is created empty for the final run (P18) and only `eval` inserts into it (`cpp/v3_engine.h:93`).
 230|   So a hit means an earlier `eval` on S in this run. If that earlier call had `emit = true` and was fresh, it offered
 231|   S. Apply the same reasoning to that earlier call; there are finitely many calls.
 232| - (c) The only `eval` with `emit = false` in the final run is the centre of the final local search (P17, P22: `false`
 233|   at `:456`). That centre is `led.hpmS`, the current running best, which is an offered model.
 234| - (d) A cache clear (P24) only turns a later hit into a fresh evaluation, which offers S again; repeated offers do not
 235|   change the store (Lemma R, Case 1).
 236| 
 237| Hence every S ∈ 𝓜_eval is offered. Finally, ∅ is offered because each block table has the code 0 (U = ∅, size
 238| 0 ≤ K, `cpp/v3_core.cpp:378-384`; its score is set at `cpp/v3_start.h:93-94`). 𝓜 ⊆ Ω is [CC] CC5
 239| (`CC_code_check.md:88-92`), re-checked at P32, P33 and P20 (:425). ∎

  57| not constant, the SMC branch was taken, and calibration returned "ok".

  59| **"The output contains a list 𝒯".** `fit$top_store` (`v3_run.R:210`), set only on completed runs. It holds
  60| `models` (original column indices, in the store order: decreasing score, ties by smaller size then lexicographic) and
  61| `value` (the score F of each model) (`cpp/v3_core.cpp:358-362`). Its capacity is 40p_ret + 1
  62| (`cpp/v3_ledger.h:78`), where p_ret is the number of non-constant predictors (`v3_preprocess.R:111-113`). So
  63| |𝒯| = min(40p_ret + 1, |𝓜|) ≤ 40p + 1. Models are distinct ([P6] Lemma R0(i)).
  64| 
  65| **"Evaluated".** A model S is *evaluated by the run* iff S ∈ 𝓜, the set of models offered to the stores of the final-run
  66| ledger ([P6] §4, Definition of 𝓜). By [P6] Lemma M, on a completed run 𝓜 is the union of three sets:
  67| - (a) every model the final run scored or re-visited: the islands' initial π₀ draws, Gibbs flips and held states, swap and
  68|   independence proposals (accepted or rejected), and every centre and scanned neighbour of the final local search and
  69|   of LS0;
  70| - (b) every block-table model;
  71| - (c) every model inherited from calibration.
  72| 
  73| In original indices, the true model S_true := {j : β*_j ≠ 0} can be evaluated only if all its columns were retained and
  74| |S_true| ≤ K. Otherwise the retention sentence is vacuous. (Remark: by [P6] Remark 6.2, a unique F-maximiser that only
  75| the calibration evaluated also ends up in 𝒯. That is a code reading and is not used.)
  76| 
  77| **"Computed in exact arithmetic".** Premise EX-A of W1-N1 ("exact scores and arithmetic",
  78| `Theory_work/Wave1/W1-N1/STATEMENT.md:70`), together with the identification (H-ID) of [P6] §0: each returned value is
  79| exactly F(S) = log ϖ(S) + log m(S), and e^{F(S)} = Z·π(S) with Z = Σ_Ω e^F and π(S) = Π(S | D_n). It is used for two
  80| things only:
  81| - (i) the weights of Π̂ are proportional to π, so Π̂ = Π(· | S ∈ 𝒯, D_n) ([P6] Lemma W);
  82| - (ii) the store order is the exact order of π, needed only for the retention sentence.
  83| 
  84| The first display uses only (i) and 𝒯 ⊆ Ω. It holds for **any** subset of Ω in place of 𝒯, however it was produced.

  86| **Π̂ (a mathematical object, not computed by the method).** Π̂ := Σ_{S∈𝒯} π_𝒯(S)Π(· | S, D_n), with π_𝒯(S) := e^{F(S)}/Σ_{S′∈𝒯}e^{F(S′)}.
  87| In the reader parametrisation (S, β, σ²) this is the same law as [P6]'s Π̂^𝒯 on (S, θ, v), pushed through the map
  88| (S, θ, v) ↦ (S, β, σ²). For each S this map is a bijection: β_j = b_j = θ_j/ŝ_j for j ∈ S and 0 off S, and σ² = v. Both θ and v are on the
  89| response scale (STATEMENT §0, `:29-39`). Under it the density attached to a draw is the same: the reader's mean
  90| ȳ + (x − x̄)ᵀβ equals â + xᵀb, since â = ȳ^r − x̄ᵀb (STATEMENT §0, `:37-39`). Hence Π̂(d_H(f, f*) > r) is the same number in

  95| Let the constants c, M₀, n₀ and the range M₀ ≤ M ≤ √n/log n be those of Theorem A, and assume (A1)–(A5) with the window
  96| q_n of this M. Let r_n := √(M·log n/n). Assume EX-A and (H-ID).

 105| ## 3. Proofs
 106| 
 107| **Proof of (C1).** Put G_n := {D_n : Π(d_H(f, f*) > r_n | D_n) ≤ n^{−cM}}. Theorem A (i) says exactly
 108| P*(Π(d_H(f, f*) > r_n | D_n) > n^{−cM}) ≤ n^{−cM}. So P*(G_n) ≥ 1 − n^{−cM}. G_n depends on the data only: Π(· | D_n) is the
 109| exact posterior, which involves no stream.
 110| 
 111| Fix D_n ∈ G_n and a completed run with π(𝒯) ≥ n^{−cM/2}. Let B := {d_H(f, f*) > r_n} ⊆ 𝚯; it is measurable by the joint
 112| measurability in [P6] Lemma P6(c). By [P6] Lemma W, π_𝒯(S) = π(S)/π(𝒯) on 𝒯 and 0 elsewhere. So Q := π_𝒯 satisfies
 113| Q(S) ≤ L·π(S) for every S ∈ Ω, with L := 1/π(𝒯) ∈ (1, ∞). Note π(𝒯) > 0 by Positivity ([P6] §0) and 𝒯 ≠ ∅ ([P6] Lemma M).
 114| Lemma P6(a) ([P6] §3) gives
 115|   Π̂(B) = QΠ(B) ≤ Π(B | D_n)/π(𝒯) ≤ n^{−cM} / n^{−cM/2} = n^{−cM/2}.
 116| Nothing in this argument depends on the streams beyond the fact that the run returned some 𝒯 ⊆ Ω with exact weights.
 117| So the bound holds for every completed run on D_n. ∎
 118| 
 119| *Relation to DIST-C.* (C1) is [P6] Proposition C-i° with Theorem A (i) in place of DIST-1 (1.1). In DIST-1's terms,
 120| t = M log n and λ = c/2: the threshold n^{−cM} = e^{−ct} and the store condition n^{−cM/2} = e^{−λt}. The P⊗ version
 121| ("P⊗(completed ∩ {π(𝒯) ≥ n^{−cM/2}} ∩ {Π̂(B) > n^{−cM/2}}) ≤ n^{−cM}") follows from (C1) by [P6] Lemma J, under any joint
 122| law whose data marginal is P*.
 123| 
 124| **Proof of (C2).** Fix the data and a completed run. "Evaluated" means S_true ∈ 𝓜 (in internal indices, through ι⁻¹).
 125| By [P6] Lemma M, 𝓜 ⊆ Ω, so S_true ∈ Ω. Since π(S_true) > ½, [P6] Lemma U shows that S_true is the unique maximiser of F
 126| over Ω. [P6] Corollary R1(ii) — which rests on Lemma R, the invariant of the coded store (`cpp/v3_ledger.h:49-57`),
 127| and on the fact that the store and the running HPM receive the same offers (`:89-94`) — gives S_true ∈ 𝒯, S_true first
 128| in the list, and Ŝ = S_true. Finally π(𝒯) ≥ π(S_true) > ½. ∎
 129| 
 130| **Last sentence of Corollary C** ("whether the list carries enough posterior probability is a property of the run
 131| that this corollary does not assert"). Consistent with the above. A sufficient condition with a probability bound
 132| needs a delivery premise: discovery of S_true ([P6] (C-ii)(α-disc): W3-SAMP D-i + Lemma PC + P-OVL) together with
 133| δ_n < ½ (selection). Without beta-min, π(𝒯) ≥ n^{−cM/2} is the premise P-STORE, with no proof and no output certificate
 134| ([P6] (C-ii)(β)).
